handover.question: Before the window-repair invoice for Flat 3, 171 Willowmere Road (Job NBL-050-2635) is paid: is it genuine, correctly priced, and for work actually carried out?
summary: Assigned provider is Stonebridge Works (event-013, event-014, event-029); the invoice email names 'Cedar Solutions' and presses for prompt payment plus a review (event-032, quoted fragment, untrusted).
Landlord approved £35 + VAT (handle) or £90 + VAT (lock) (event-019, event-021); the recorded figure is £49.40 incl VAT (event-037) — matches neither.

The only booked visit was 10:00-16:00 on 08/07/2024 (event-028, event-029, event-030), yet the invoice arrived 03/07 (event-032, event-035) and completion was reported to the landlord 04/07 (event-036).

options: Hold payment; ask Stonebridge Works in writing to confirm attendance date, part fitted and that the invoice is theirs, and reconcile £49.40 against the approved £35 + VAT; pay only if it reconciles.
Pay as invoiced on the normal cycle and reconcile afterwards — fastest, but risks paying an unverified third party for work with no evidence of attendance.
Treat as suspected invoice fraud now: freeze the payee record, report internally, and re-inspect the window with a different contractor.
handover.recommended: Hold payment and obtain written confirmation from Stonebridge Works on payee, amount and attendance date, alongside the tenant's reply (ACT-2), before anything is paid.

handover.undo: Nothing irreversible done by me: no payment, no new work order. The closure (event-043) can be reopened; the tenant has only been asked to confirm attendance and that the window secures.
